subject.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces

question: Should the final control-plane audit contract land through this broader PR, through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100965, or be split so this PR only owns plugin command-surface auditing?
rationale: Two external security-audit PRs modify the same operator-facing control-plane audit contract with different check IDs, and this PR also changes plugin command-surface audit behavior under a protected security label.

options.title: Split Scope After Fixes
options.body: Let the focused control-plane PR own that audit check once mergeable, and require this PR to fix upgrade-safe plugin command metadata plus real audit proof before continuing as the plugin command-surface change.

options.title: Make This PR Canonical
options.body: Use this broader PR as the single landing path only after it fixes the stale-registry false-negative, supplies real audit proof, and reconciles the check ID with the focused PR.

options.title: Pause Both For Security Contract Review
options.body: Hold both PRs until security owners choose the stable check IDs, severities, and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Split Scope After Fixes
recommendation.body: Let the focused control-plane PR own that audit check once mergeable, and require this PR to fix upgrade-safe plugin command metadata plus real audit proof before continuing as the plugin command-surface change.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest feature-history signal for the existing exposure-matrix audit behavior this PR extends.
